answer: Device-bound identity stops sybil farming at the hardware layer. Each identity must present a fresh attestation from a trusted execution enclave keyed to one physical device, so one machine vouches for one identity. At the zenith of a wave an attacker needs one device per fake, about $80 each, so 1,000 fakes cost $80,000 in hardware. The tide turns because enclave keys cannot be copied, and a device caught attesting twice is burned from the registry. That proof is the bridge to a trust score no new fake can buy. Limit: a funded device farm can enter, so pair it with behavior checks.
